subtasks.title: Guard lazy shift-open + ShiftStart emit against force-login impersonators in status()
subtasks.approach: In ClarityScoutShiftController::status(), before calling $this->ensureOpenShift->currentOpenForKit($kit), branch on $user->isScoutForceImpersonator(). When true, do NOT call currentOpenShift/currentOpenForKit and do NOT emit ShiftStart analytics or the audit log; return the exact same 'no open shift' JSON payload the controller already returns when currentOpenForKit yields no open shift (shift_id null, open false, started_at/ended_at/end_type null — match the real shape in the file, do not invent keys). Normal (non-impersonator) drivers take the unchanged existing path. Use the existing User::isScoutForceImpersonator() SoT — do not inline a fresh token-ability check. TDD: write the pinning tests first (red), then add the guard (green).
subtasks.intended_diffs: ClarityScoutShiftController::status(): add an early impersonator branch that returns the no-open-shift payload without touching EnsureOpenShift/Analytics/audit. Test file: (a) impersonator token ['*','clarity-scout-force'] + fresh matching Postgres scan activity + no existing kit_shifts row -> GET /shift/status returns no-open-shift shape, KitShift::count() unchanged, Analytics::track NEVER called with ShiftStart; (b) regression: normal ['clarity-scout'] token + same scan activity -> a kit_shifts row IS created (wasRecentlyCreated) and Analytics::track fires ShiftStart once.
